title: Resident Evil Studio That’s Making Nintendo’s Zelda Movie Now Gunning For Battlefield As Well
description: Video games are the new battlefield for movie ideas, and after a reported bidding war, it appears Sony Pictures is the frontrunner to secure the rights to the Battlefield movie. The Wrap reported that Sony Pictures was in the lead position to win the rights, and The Hollywood Reporter backed this up. The Battlefield movie package reportedly includes Mission: Impossible director Christopher McQuarrie behind the camera, with Oscar-winner Michael B. Jordan in the mix to star and produce it. McQuarrie is also writing and producing. Universal, Netflix, Amazon MGM Studios, and Warner Bros. Discovery (now operating under Skydance) all reportedly submitted bids for the Battlefield movie. The Wrap said the dealmaking process is "shaping up to be the biggest bidding war of the year." The report did not mention any dollar numbers attached to the bids, or any other particulars, however. For example, if Netflix closes the deal, many might expect the film to be released on streaming instead of theatrically (but even at Netflix these days that's not a certainty). In the video game landscape, Battlefield and Call of Duty are rivals, and now they could become film foes, too. Skydance is making a Call of Duty movie, with Sicario's Taylor Sheridan writing and Lone Survivor's Peter Berg directing. The latest Battlefield game, meanwhile, was 2025's Battlefield 6, which was the year's best-selling game overall in the US, surpassing Activision's Call of Duty: Black Ops 7. EA and Battlefield Studios will continue to support the game with more updates and new content into 2027. In 2024, Battlefield boss Vince Zampella--who has since passed away--said EA had held discussions about a Battlefield movie or TV show already. A decade ago, Paramount bought the rights to make a Battlefield TV show, but it never materialized. In 2012, Fox was developing an hour-long comedy show based on the Battlefield: Bad Company series, with Adam Sandler's company signed on. This show also did not come to…

title: Love And Deepspace Devs Have One Simple Request: Please Don’t Drink The Poison
description: It hasn't been an easy year for the Love and Deepspace community after the Valko controversy left the fandom divided, but it looks like developer Papergames has brewed up new trouble for the gacha game. A few days ago, the developer posted cocktail recipes online, and followers quickly warned the studio that recreating those drinks could result in lethal concoctions. "One taste of this Special Blend and you won’t forget it," the original post read, which was accompanied by recipes for the non-alcoholic cocktail mixes. Each one is inspired by an in-game slime--Artsyblobbu, Fiendyblobbu, Pilotblobbu, Snowyblobbu, and Stellablobbu--and the list of ingredients includes several items found inside of Love and Deepspace. Cute, wholesome fun, right? Not exactly. As people online pointed out, some of those ingredients include hallucinogens like Datura and other toxic elements like colchicine, which you definitely should not be consuming. Papergames released a follow-up post a day later. They stressed that the drink recipes posted above are "fictional" and for "in-game purposes" only. The replies to the cocktail tweets have been just as toxic, with several Love and Deepspace players quickly hijacking the thread to demand that the hunky werewolf Valko be finally added to the game--which is an entirely different can of worms. Long story short: Think twice before you start mixing drinks from a video game social media account, as it pays to double-check the ingredients so that you don't harm your body or start tripping the light fantastic.

title: You Can Grab Sonic X Shadow Generations Cheaper Than Steam’s Fall Sale, But You Gotta Go Fast
description: After years of being a Sonic fan and suffering gut punch after gut punch with every new entry in the franchise, the blue blur has finally been on a roll. Sorry, that joke was awful, but it is true—the movies have been overwhelmingly successful, Sonic Frontiers was an interesting take on the formula, and while the latest “typical” game is a remaster in some ways, Sonic X Shadow Generations is one of the greatest Sonic experiences in years. Thankfully, you can skip past Steam’s Green Hills and get straight into the best part, as Fanatical has it cheaper than Valve’s Fall sale right now. The “Sonic” part of Sonic X Shadow Generations is the familiar part. It is functionally the same as the 2011 original, seeing modern Sonic and classic Sonic combine forces against an entity called the Time Eater. With their friends scattered across different eras, the pair race off to save the world. The new version has improved visuals and some adjusted cutscenes, but the general consensus in our Sonic Generations review way back at launch remains consistent with this latest take. What is more interesting, however, is the new Shadow Generations story. Running (pun intended) parallel with the story of Sonic Generations, this new campaign sees Shadow deal with his old rival, Black Doom. After being stuck in the White Space, the villain grants Shadow some new abilities in the form of Doom Powers, which make elements of the familiar Sonic-style levels even more engaging. Sadly, he doesn’t have his guns this time. As someone who fell in love with the edginess of Shadow back when I was a wee little boy, his guns being gone doesn’t matter to me. In fact, Shadow is arguably way cooler now than he has ever been, and his new abilities make the standard Sonic affair even more exciting. Shadow Generations has only added to the 2011 original, and now I wouldn’t be able to play the 15-year-old version of the game because it would feel empty without the black-and-red hedgehog. Right now, the game…

title: "Coders will never forgive me for this level": Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 has a rotatable "fleshmetal" puzzle map that drove its own development team crazy
description: In the grim darkness of the far future, there is something far worse than war. There is: a level that is basically a huge, spinning lock full of tentacles, with your Space Marine or Sister of Battle protagonist naturally serving as the key. Auroch Digital's new FPS Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 launches next week, and I've been chatting to the game's principal designer Matt Bone about some of the more "creative" environments in store. It's a sturdy rule of thumb that all the best ideas in gamedev are the ones that make your colleagues want to fill your trousers with sea urchins. Bone certainly appears to have achieved this with the map comfortingly known as Vicious Circles. Read more

title: This week in PC games: Star Wars: Galactic Racer, Hellraiser: Revival, and a throwback tycoon game about turning utopias into carparks
description: Happy this week, all! I regret to inform you that the videogame developers have been at it again. Sometimes, I find that the promising new releases distribute themselves evenly throughout the week, like butter perfectly spread over just the right amount of toast. And sometimes, as with this week's haul, they congregate weirdly on Thursday and Friday. It's as though they were trying to get away from me, like rats ambushed in the pantry, pawing frantically against the weekend's closed and bolted door. Haha! Hahahaaha! There is no escape, cheese-filching squeakmonsters! Down you go! Down you go into the Maw! If you think characterising new videogames as a rodent infestation is unkind, I quite agree. Rats are sociable, adaptable, and admirable creatures who deserve better than to be compared to stupid videogames. In any case, I am only being macabre because this is the month of Halloween – hence the conspicuous abundance of horror in the list below. Read more

title: Nivalis Nights dares to ask what if Cyberpunk 2077 met Dave the Diver and Stardew Valley? And for now at least I'm loving the answer
description: As I throw open the windows on my first day in Nivalis, breathing in the city's neon-streaked air and watching the smog roil across the blackened sky, my government-mandated AI automata informs me the district is in lockdown and a serial killer's on the loose. Five hours later, I've become embroiled in a child trafficking plot (the good kind, apparently, seeing as I'm helping them get out ); I've stumbled across an oil rig and befriended its city separatists; I've inadvertently struck up a romance with a CorpSec agent who's trying to shut down my noodle bar; and I've met a woman who writes new childhoods for condemned criminals, in the city's hope that implanting them will make 'em behave. All this and I've only grown a single onion. Nivalis Nights, it's fair to say, is not your average farm-life sim. Read more

title: The Sunday Papers
description: Sundays are for having the first lie-in in a month. No trips to visit family, no waking in unfamiliar beds, and, best of all, no having to wait until the hosts are up before you can get started on breakfast. I will be snoozing deeply in my own particular mattress before having a plate of toast and scrambled eggs at a time that I deem appropriate. Once that's all polished away, I will return to bed with a fresh cup of coffee and peruse the week's best writing at my own leisure. What's that? You want me to share? Fine. You can have a read of them when I'm done. Read more
